cards.explanation: The answer is gate. God says, "Stand in the gate of the house of the LORD and proclaim this message…" (Jeremiah 7:2). Then He tells Jeremiah who to address: "…all you people of Judah who enter through these gates to worship the LORD." That's a message with a very clear address on it, friends.

The answer is True. God says, "Correct your ways and deeds, and I will let you live in this place." (Jeremiah 7:3). He puts the way forward right at the start of the message. That's a door held wide open, friends.

The answer is the temple of the LORD. God spells out the deceptive words: "This is the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD." (Jeremiah 7:4). Same line, three times. I think they were hoping the repeating would make it hold more weight.

The answer is acting justly toward one another. God says, "…if you act justly toward one another…" (Jeremiah 7:5). He's talking about how they treat each other, not just how they act when they come to worship. The list that follows gets even more specific, friends.

The answer is False. God doesn't say they can keep following other gods. He lists it right alongside the rest: "…if you no longer oppress the foreigner and the fatherless and the widow, and if you no longer shed innocent blood in this place or follow other gods to your own harm…" (Jeremiah 7:6). It's a package, not a pick-and-choose, bakers.

The answer is that they're delivered so they can keep going. God asks if they will come stand before Him in His house and say, "We are delivered, so we can continue with all these abominations…" (Jeremiah 7:10). Read that slowly, friends. It's a get-out-of-trouble card, with the permission to keep going built right in. God holds up that picture and asks if it makes sense.

The answer is a den of robbers. God asks, "Has this house, which bears My Name, become a den of robbers in your sight?" (Jeremiah 7:11). Then He adds, "Yes, I too have seen it…" That's the picture He chooses, and He says He has seen it too.

The answer is True. God tells them to go to Shiloh and "…see what I did to it because of the wickedness of My people Israel." (Jeremiah 7:12). He names the reason Himself, bakers. It's right there in the verse, so we don't have to guess.

The answer is False. God says, "…I have spoken to you again and again but you would not listen, and I have called to you but you would not answer…" (Jeremiah 7:13). Again and again, plus calling on top of it. He kept reaching out to them, friends.

The answer is house. God says, "…what I did to Shiloh I will now do to the house that bears My Name, the house in which you trust…" (Jeremiah 7:14). The very place they were leaning on is the place He's talking about, friends. I think that stings.

The answer is that God will cast them out of His presence. He says, "And I will cast you out of My presence, just as I have cast out all your brothers, all the descendants of Ephraim." (Jeremiah 7:15). This is a heavy line, and it's okay to let it sit for a second. Then keep going, friends, because the story isn't over.
